sections.h2: Which Sherburne County offices deal with my tax bill?
sections.html:
Two departments handle it, and they share one suite in Elk River. Valuation and classification belong to the Assessor (763-765-4900). Billing and collection belong to the Auditor/Treasurer (763-765-4350). The street address for both is 13880 Business Center Drive NW, Suite 100, Elk River, MN 55330-4668.

The county describes the Auditor/Treasurer's job as working out tax rates, preparing statements and the "truth in taxation" notices, and tracking every levy from towns, cities and schools. When a parcel falls behind, that same department takes judgment and starts forfeiture under state law. Think of the Assessor as the office for arguing about worth, and the Auditor/Treasurer as the office for learning what you owe on the day you list the house.

sections.h2: What kind of county is Sherburne for a seller?
sections.html:
Sherburne belongs to the Minneapolis-St. Paul metropolitan statistical area and counts Elk River as both seat and biggest city. Of its 451 square miles, 433 are land. Low hills, scattered lakes and sandy, gravelly glacial soil make up the terrain, and that soil is less suited to farming than much of Minnesota. The Mississippi forms the southern boundary and the Rum River cuts through the upper east side.

County government began at Humboldt, the village that later took the name Big Lake, before a county vote moved the seat to Elk River in 1867. Incorporated cities now include Baldwin, Becker, Big Lake, Clear Lake, Elk River and Zimmerman, with Princeton and St. Cloud partly inside the line. Census QuickFacts supplies the housing picture:

  • Population reached 104,194 in July 2025, a 7.2% rise over the April 2020 base.
  • The county holds 38,457 housing units, and owners live in 83.2% of the occupied ones.
  • A typical owned home was worth $361,400 across 2020 to 2024.
  • The usual household brings in $105,466 a year and drives 30.7 minutes to work.
  • Renters pay about $1,127 a month in gross rent, and households average 2.78 people across 35,555 homes.
  • Builders pulled 319 permits in 2025 across roughly 225 residents per square mile.

Lakes, rivers and the Sherburne National Wildlife Refuge all lie within the county, so setting can move a parcel's value as much as the house does.

sections.h2: When do Sherburne County property taxes come due, and what do late payments cost?
sections.html:
Mark May 15 and October 15. Farmland owners get until November 15 for the second half. The county counts a mailed check as on time only if the postmark falls on or before the deadline, and it cautions that many post offices now stamp mail two or three days after pickup. A real estate bill of $50 or less has just one deadline, May 15.

Penalties begin the day after each deadline and rise month by month. This is the 2026 schedule for a first half left unpaid:

Sherburne County first-half penalty by date, 2026 (county Penalties page)

An unpaid second half starts at 2% for homesteads and 4% for everything else on October 16. Farm homesteads that miss the November deadline owe 6%, and non-homestead farmland owes 8%. Owners paying late should ask the property tax division for the exact penalty before sending money.

sections.h2: What are my options for paying Sherburne County tax?
sections.html:
The county's payment page lays out five routes. Checks go to the Sherburne County Auditor / Treasurer at the Elk River address. The property tax division in the Government Center also takes cash or check at the counter, and a drop box by the main entrance (door A) stays open after hours.

  • Forte, online or at 877-690-3729 with jurisdiction code 3307: 2.40% of the tax (minimum $2.00) on credit cards, $1.55 per eCheck, $4.00 on a debit card. Keep the parcel ID handy.
  • Direct payment: withdrawals on May 15 and October 15, or November 15 for farmland. Forms must arrive by April 15 for the spring withdrawal and September 15 for the fall one, and a cancellation has to meet those same cutoffs.
  • Lender escrow: if your mortgage payment includes tax, the lender sends it. Confirm with your servicer.

A withdrawal that lands on a weekend or bank holiday happens the following business day.

sections.h2: How can I contest a Sherburne County value or class?
sections.html:
Gather evidence first, such as a recent appraisal or sales of similar homes, and talk it over with the Assessor. If that does not settle things, attend the local board shown on your valuation notice. The county's 2026 list ran from early April, when Big Lake and Princeton hearings took place at the Government Center on April 3, to Livonia Township on April 27, so this year's round is over.

  • Local board: meets at the city or township hall in April, with the exact date printed on your notice.
  • County board: sat Tuesday, June 16 in 2026 at 3:00 p.m., by appointment only, arranged through the Auditor/Treasurer at 763-765-4351.
  • Minnesota Tax Court: you may petition directly after receiving the notice, up to April 30 of the year the tax is payable (court phone 651-296-2806).

Next spring's notice will carry the new dates. The Assessor also runs an online tool at gis.co.sherburne.mn.us/AssessmentSchedule that shows the year an appraiser will inspect an address, since every property needs a physical review once in five years.

The Assessor's property values page explains what is being tested. Minnesota statutes call for estimated market value to sit at 100% of market, so appraisers review current sales continuously and note any physical change that affects land or buildings. A new deck, a finished basement or a demolished garage all belong in the conversation, because they alter what the appraiser should have on file.

Errors discovered afterward can be corrected through an abatement request to the Assessor. The county lists three kinds: homestead (you must show you lived there), valuation and classification, and a local option for a house where disaster damage reaches half the structure's value. Pay on schedule meanwhile, because review can take months.

sections.h2: How does a sale change my Sherburne County tax responsibilities?
sections.html:
Any unpaid balance gets cleared at the closing table, normally out of your proceeds. Phone the Auditor/Treasurer for the amount due on the parcel, and ask your lender what sits in escrow if one collects your tax.

Selling a homesteaded house also creates a duty. The county cites Minnesota Statute 273.124, subdivision 13 (e): report the sale, transfer or change of primary residence to the Assessor within 30 days. An online change-of-address form is posted on the county site. Request a copy of the current statement from the Auditor/Treasurer too, as the title company will want the parcel figures.

faqs.q: Which dates should I remember for Sherburne County real estate tax?
faqs.a: May 15 and October 15, with agricultural parcels paying the second half on November 15. A bill of $50 or less is entirely due May 15. Postmarks decide whether a mailed check is on time.

faqs.q: What is the Sherburne County Assessor's phone number?
faqs.a: 763-765-4900. The office works from 13880 Business Center Drive NW, Suite 100, Elk River, and it deals with value, class, abatements and the opening stage of any appeal.

faqs.q: Does Sherburne County accept credit cards for tax?
faqs.a: Yes, through Forte online or by calling 877-690-3729 with jurisdiction code 3307. Expect 2.40% on credit cards with a $2.00 floor, $1.55 on eChecks and $4.00 on debit cards, shown before you confirm.

faqs.q: Where does a county board of appeal hearing take place in Sherburne County?
faqs.a: At the Sherburne County Government Center in Elk River. Owners who stayed unhappy after their local board must book through the Auditor/Treasurer at 763-765-4351. In 2026 it met June 16.

faqs.q: What must I report after selling my Sherburne County homestead?
faqs.a: Tell the Assessor within 30 days, as Minnesota Statute 273.124, subdivision 13 (e), requires. Call 763-765-4900 with questions.
